full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J: This Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Artha Rin Suit No. 291 of 2003 (Annexure-A) in the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2 Dhaka should not be declared to have been instituted and proceeded with in violation of relevant provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and thereby the judgment and decree passed should not be declared to be illegal and without lawful authority.

2. The defendant No. 2 is the Managing Director of Desh Steel Limited involved in the business of steel re-rolling. It is stated that for construction of a 2,150 square feet flat on the second floor of a six-storied residential building situated at House No. 16, Road No. 16/A, Gulshan, Dhaka, the present petitioner obtained home mortgage loan of Taka 30,00,000 on 15-4-2000 from the respondent No. 1 vide sanction letter dated 7-3-2000 subject to the condition of repayment of the same within 15 years and paid 12 post-dated cherubs at the rate of Taka 44,315 each against repayment and also by giving equitable mortgage of properties as per loan agreement. It is further stated that out of the sanctioned loan of Taka 30,00,000 the present petitioner and the defendant No. 2 together drew Taka 29,00,000 and repaid Taka 6,87,200 and defaulted in further repayment, for which, the plaintiff being a financial institution instituted the Artha Rin Suit No. 291 of 2003 for recovery of Taka 38,15,261 before the respondent No. 2, the Adalat.

3. The suit was instituted against 8 defendants including the present petitioner and his wife. But only defendant No. 7 contested the suit and rest did not. However, the suit has been decreed by the trial Court on contest against the defendant No. 7 and ex parte against the rest directing the defendants to repay the loan amount of Taka 38,15,261 to the plaintiff bank within 60 days in default the plaintiff will be at liberty to realise the same from the defendants in accordance with law. The decree was put into auction by the plaintiff in Execution Case No. 450 of 2004. Therein the judgment debtor Nos. 1 and 2 entered appearance and prayed for time to file written objection and ultimately, on 30-5-2005, the judgment debtor filed an application for extension of time to file written objection but the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat rejected the said application when they were found not present on call and fixed 25-6-2005 for steps to be taken under section 33(1) of the AM. At this stage the petitioner, without preferring any appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, filed this writ petition under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule on 23-7-2005 contending that section 12(1) of the Ain 2003 has put restriction in preferring any suit for recovery of loan.

4. The Rule was duly served upon the two respondents. Moreover, the respondent No. 1, the financial institution, contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition denying the material allegations of the writ petition contending, inter alia, that since in the present Rule the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat has been challenged the same is not maintainable on the ground that in the case of Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank and others, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6, it has been held by the Appellate Division that since special provision for appeal has been made against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat no application under Article 102 lies against such judgment and decree. Secondly, since no Power of Attorney was given by the mortgagor in favour of the mortgagee institution to sell the mortgaged property, hence, section 12 of the Ain is not applicable in the present case. He also referred to the case of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank and others reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191 wherein it has been held "the suit against the petitioner being barred by limitation and in excess of the Court's jurisdiction are matters to be agitated in appeal and not under the writ jurisdiction". Hence, the Rule should be discharged.

5. Mr GS Huq, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits firstly, that section 12(1), (2) and (3) of the AM, 2003 clearly provides that no financial institution shall file any suit in the Artha Rin Adalat before selling the mortgaged property in auction by advertisement of sale, if there be any residue only that remaining portion can be recovered by instituting a suit in the Artha Rin Adalat. Since the petitioner has already mortgaged his six-stored building to the respondent No. 1 thus, without complying with the provision of section 12 of the Ain the filing of the suit is without any lawful authority. As such, the proceeding of the suit having been continued in the said Adalat and decreeing the suit without complying with the provision of section 12(6) is volatile of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution, for which, this writ petition is maintainable. He next submits that section 12(6) clearly provides that in case the provision of section 12(2) and (3) are not complied with the Artha Rin Adalat in its own motion and or on the application of the judgment debtor, will deduct the value of the mortgaged property, where the value of the property mortgaged has been determined by the financial institution or in case no value has been determined then upon obtaining the value of the same from the local Sub-Registrar's Office deduct the same from the plaintiffs claim in the suit and decree the suit accordingly. He submits that the Adalat in spite of such provision of law did not take any such step under section 12(6) of the Ain hence, the judgment and decree passed by the Adalat is perverse, nullity, illegal and without any basis. As such, putting the petitioner into jeopardy to undergo the harsh provision of challenging the judgment and decree by depositing 50% of the decretal amount, which he would not have to face if the property was sold under section 12 or if the learned Adalat would have applied section 12(6) and the amount being adjusted with the claim. Because the value of the mortgaged property is much more higher than the claim of the plaintiff institution. He further submits that Order XX, rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides as to what should be the contents of a decree. But the decree passed in the instant suit also lacks all those requirements. As such, the judgment and decree is nothing but a void and a non-existent decree and, as such, is a nullity in the eye of law. He lastly, submits that the decision of the Appellate Division in 46 DLR and 54 DLR (as referred by the respondent) are given under the old Ain of 1990 which has been repealed by the new Ain of 2003 and, as such, cannot be applied in the cases which are governed by the new law. Accordingly, he submits that though under Article 111 of the Constitution the decisions of the Appellate Division are binding upon the High Court Division but the aforesaid decisions being delivered over the repealed law the same cannot be applied in the present case. In this respect, he referred to the provision of section 6 of the General Clauses Act and submits that the writ petition is very much maintainable and the Rule should be made absolute.

6. On the other hand, Mr M Morshed Ahmed Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 1 submits firstly, that the decisions in 46 DLR and 54 DLR by the Appellate Division though given under the repealed law but the principle laid down in those two decisions are binding upon the High Court Division under Article 111 of the Constitution and, pursuant to those two decisions, this writ petition is not maintainable. He submits that it is clear and well settled by now that the petitioner has the remedy against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat under the provision of the Artha Rin Adalat AM itself and in this respect depositing 50% of the decretal amount cannot be said to be an unreasonable restriction. This view was, also, taken by another Bench of this Division in the case of Abdul Gaffar Chowdhury vs Judge Artha Rin Adalat and others. So, preliminary issue as to maintainability of the writ petition is in favour of the respondent. Mr Khan next submits that section 6 of the General Clauses Act does not hold good in the present case. He next submits that the whole submission of the petitioner is that without complying with the provision of section 12 of the Ain the suit cannot be instituted. But section 12(3) provides that where the borrower, at the time of mortgaging the property, executed a power of attorney giving power to the mortgagee institution to sell the same then only the provision of section 12 can be attracted. But, in the present case, the petitioner did not execute any such power of attorney in favour of the respondent institution. In this respect, he referred to paragraph No. 10 of the plaint (Annexure-A) and submits that in the said paragraph the plaintiff has categorically stated the class of documents lying with the plaintiff which have been executed and submitted by the defendant petitioner and it is clear there from that there is no mention of such power of attorney which has neither been executed by the defendant-petitioner nor filed by the respondent institution So, the question of compliance of section 12 does not arise at all in this particular case. His next submission as to applicability of section 12(6) is that the sub-section (6) cannot be read is elatedly because the same is dependent on sub-sections (2) and (3) and since there is no compliance of section 12(2) or (3) so no question arises at all to apply section 12(6) of the Ain. So the Adalat though was given power to adjust the value of the mortgaged property and deduct the same from the claim of the plaintiff but such power is to be exercised subject to sub-section (3) of the Ain. Since no such power to sell the property has been given the respondent institution was not in a position to comply with the section 12(3) and since section 12(3) was not complied with and the mortgaged property could not be sold in auction there was no scope for the Adalat to exercise any power under section 12(6). So, the contention of the petitioner as to passing the decree without complying with section 12 of the Ain has no legal basis. As to other submission of Mr Huq on section 6 of the General Clauses Act Mr Khan contends that since the petitioner did not take any such ground in the writ petition he cannot agree with the same under the present circumstances of the case. Even then Mr Khan contended that the repealed law, 'Ain' 1990, has not been applied in the present case but the decision given by the Appellate Division relating to the principle laid down therein applies. The principle being that the appeal is the only forum provided by both the statutes to challenge judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat and writ does not lie. So, the contention of Mr Hoq as to applicability of General Clauses Act has no basis in this case. On the question of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution, Mr Khan submits that this question has been well taken care of by the Appellate Division as well as by the High Court Division in many other cases exercising writ jurisdiction. He lastly, submits that all the grounds taken in this Rule may be good grounds for the petitioner in appeal if so prefers but such cannot be agitated under this constitutional jurisdiction as decided in 46 DLR case and, as such, this Rule should be discharged.

7. We have perused the writ petition along with the annexure, the affidavit-in-opposition and the law referred to hereinabove. The questions in this writ petition are firstly, on the maintainability of the writ petition. Secondly, as to non compliance of the provision of section 12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and thus, requires to see whether the proceeding of the suit and, the judgment and decree passed therein is in accordance with law. Thirdly, whether the decree is in accordance with Order XX, rule 6 of Code of Civil Procedure and, if not, whether the same is a nullity in the eye of law and lastly, whether the decisions of the Appellate Division passed under the old Ain is applicable in the case proceeded with under the new Ain.

<u>8. The first question as to maintainability of the writ petition challenging the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in the Artha Rin Suit has been taken care of firstly, in the case of Chandpur Jute Suppliers and others vs Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Chandpur and others, reported in 2 BLC 49. Therein the High Court Division categorically held "all the borrowers of the financial institutions are treated on the same footing as they are at liberty to take protection of section 6(2) or section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain for setting aside an ex parte decree or preferring an appeal, it cannot be said that such borrowers have lost the protection of law or to be treated in accordance with law as enshrined in Article 31 of the Constitution." In that decision, it has further been held "it is now well settled that an appeal is a creature of the statute and unless the statute makes any provision for appeal there is no right of appeal." While deciding the said case the said Division Bench also relied on another decision given by another Bench of the High Court Division which was challenged before the Appellate Division in CPLA No. 359 of 1991 and was dismissed upon upholding the summary rejection order of the High Court Division on the ground of availability of the alternative remedy provided by law. (CPLA No. 359 of 1991 is the Zahirul Islam's case which has been reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191). Therein it has been held that deposit of 50% of the decretal dues at the time of preferring of appeal is the condition of appeal in a regular suit which cannot be equated with any other law. So, when there is an alternative remedy by way of appeal under section 7 of the old law or under section 41 of the present law, the judgment and decree passed by the Adalat cannot be challenged under the writ jurisdiction. This view has also been taken in the case of Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6. So, as to maintainability of the writ petition we are of the view that the petitioner being a defendant in the suit having not contested the same, preferring of the writ petition without availing the forum of appeal as provided under section 41 of the Ain or challenging the ex parte decree under section 19 of the Ain, the writ petition is not maintainable.</u>

<u>9. On the second question as to filing of the suit, proceeding and disposal of the same by the Artha Rin Adalat without complying with the provision of section 12 of the Ain is lawful, we are to see the language of the law. In this respect, sections 12(1), (2), (3), (4), (6) and (7) of the Ain are required to be looked into which reads as follows:</u>

<u>“১২। আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক কতিপয় জামানত বিক্রয় । (১) উপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, কোন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান, উহার নিজ দখল বা নিয়ন্ত্রণে থাকা বিবাদীর কোন সম্পত্তি যাহা পন বা বন্ধক (Lien or Plege) ঋণ প্রদান করা হইয়াছে, এবং যাহা বিক্রয় করিবার আইনগত অধিকার রহিয়াছে বা বাদীকে অর্পন করা হইয়াছে <u>উহা বিক্রয় না করিয়া এবং বিক্রয়লব্ধ অর্থ ঋণ পরিশোধ</u> বাবদ সমন্বয় না করিয়া অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে কোন মামলা দায়ের করিবে না।</u>

<u>(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর বিধান সত্ত্বেও কোন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান নিজ দখল বা নিয়ন্ত্রনে থাকা ঋণ বা বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় না করিয়া মামলা দায়ের করিলে অনতিবিলম্বে উক্ত সম্পত্তি পূর্ব বর্ণিত মতে বিক্রয় বিক্রয়লব্ধ অর্থ ঋনের সহিত সমন্বয়ে করিবে এবং বিষয়টি আদালতকে লিখিতভাবে অবহিত করিবে।</u>

<u>(৩) কোন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান বিবাদীর নিকট হইতে কোন স্থাবর সম্পত্তি (Immovable Property) বন্ধক (Mortgage)রাখিয়া অথবা অস্থাবর সম্পত্তি (Movable Property) দায়বদ্ধ রাখিয়া (Hypothecated) ঋণ প্রদান করিলে এবং বন্ধক প্রদান বা দায়বদ্ধ রাখার সময় বন্ধকী বা দায়বদ্ধ সম্পত্তি বিক্রয়ের ক্ষমতা (Power of Attorney) আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানকে প্রদান ক���া হইয়া থাকিলে <u>উহা বিক্রয় না করিয়া এবং বিক্রয়লব্ধ অর্থ ঋণ পরিশোধ</u> বাবদ সমন্বয় না করিয়া অথবা বিক্রয়ের চেষ্টা করিয়া ব্যর্থ না হইয়া অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে কোন মামলা দায়ের করিবে না।</u>

<u>(৪) উপ-ধারা (৩) এ উল্লেখিত বিক্রয়ের ক্ষেত্রে আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান এই আইনের ধারা ৩৩ এর উপধারা (১), (২) ‍ও (৩) এর বিধান যতদুর সম্ভব অনুসরন করিবে।</u>

<u>From a reading of the aforesaid provision of law it is clear that in this particular case section 12(3) is the appropriate section which could be attracted. But from a reading of the plaint it appears that no such power has been given by the petitioner under section 12(3) of the Ain. As such, the provision of selling the mortgaged property in auction under section 12(4) is not applicable in the present case. Hence, if section 12(2),(3) and 4 are not applicable then there is no question of selling the property tinder section 12(4) on the ground that the plaintiff did not give any power to sell the mortgaged property and in case no such power is given or sale takes place there is no question of adjusting the sale proceeds with the claim under section 12(6) and file a suit for the rest of the amount. No such situation has been created to attract section 12(6) of the Ain because sub-section (6) started with</u>

<u>firstly, the mortgagee is required to have a power executed by the mortgagor to sell and upon having such power the mortgagee is to sell the mortgaged property and then to adjust the sale proceeds with the actual claim. If the mortgagee does not have the power to sell under sub-section (3) then sub-section (6) does not come into operation. In the present case, no question of compliance of section 12(6) arises and no such situation was made for which the Adalat of its own motion could apply sub-section (6). So, the submissions of the petitioner as to determination of the value of the mortgaged property and deduct sale proceeds from the claim of the plaintiff and decree the suit on the residue, if there be any, does not arise at all. Moreover, the petitioner did not apply under section 12(6) of the Ain to deduct the value of the mortgaged property from the claim of the suit and, as such, cannot claim of the suit now that the decree is a nullity. So, the submission of Mr Huq as to non application of section 12(6) has left the petitioner in a position that he was not treated equally does not arise at all.</u>

<u>10. On the question of applicability of the decisions of the Appellate Division passed under the repealed Ain in the case proceeded with under the new Ain it is required to mention that the Article 111 of the Constitution clearly provides "the law declared by the Appellate Division shall be binding on the High Court Division and the law declared by either Division of the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts subordinate to it. In the aforesaid two decisions referring to the provision of section 7 of the Ain of 1990, the Appellate Division categorically declared that where the statute provides specific forum of appeal no writ lies challenging the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. The provision of appeal has been specifically given in section 7 of the Ain of 1990 which is the provision of appeal under section 41 of the Ain of 2003. So, the law is settled by the Appellate Division that where the specific provision for appeal is available or provided in the statute no writ lies. There is no question as to appeal under the old Ain or under the new Ain. Question is, whether the statute provides the forum of appeal. Admittedly, both the repealed and the new Ains provide forum of appeal, of course, under two different sections but the provision is for challenging the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat in appeal. That being the adequate alternative remedy provided under Article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution, under which the petitioner has come, cannot be attracted. So, the contention of Mr Hoque is not sustainable. The submission of Mr GS Huq as to applicability of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, it is found upon reading the said provision that the said submission is a misconceived one and not tenable in the eye of law.</u>

<u>11. The other question as to passing of the decree without complying with Order XX, rule 6 of the Code could have been good grounds for agitating before the Court of appeal. But without contesting the suit and without applying section 19 of the Ain for setting aside the ex parte decree or without applying for deduction of the value from the claim the suit as provided in section 12(6) of the Ain the petitioner cannot now come under the writ jurisdiction and claim that the proceeding and the judgment and decree delivered by the Artha Rin Adalat is a nullity and/or void and without any basis.</u>
